clue.text: Damp home for China's last chairman's supporter?

indicators.note: a home holds its occupant, so the damp word houses the letter placed inside it

parts.note: damp means slightly wet

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the country's name is kept

parts.note: the final letter of China

explanation.surface: A soggy residence for the last leader of China, or perhaps a question about where his followers live.
explanation.walkthrough: The chairman is Chairman Mao, so his supporter is a follower of his political thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong, China's Communist leader known as Chairman Mao, is called by his name plus the usual -ist suffix.

clue.text: Engage in experiment involving rattlesnake's skin

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so the experiment wraps around the snake's outer letters

parts.note: a test is an experiment

indicators.note: a skin is the outside layer, so only the outer letters of the snake are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of rattlesnake

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a scientific trial that uses the skin shed by a rattlesnake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engage in' looks like a phrase; the definition is just 'Engage', and 'in' supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to engage their attention, holding it and making them curious.

clue.text: Fellow with short list of things to be done with a stub

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the list loses its final letter

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

parts.words: list of things to be done
parts.note: an agenda is a list of items to deal with

explanation.surface: A man carries a brief to-do list for dealing with a leftover stub of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette, so the fag end is the butt left after smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: The burnt-down remnant of a cigarette is its stub, and figuratively the last unimportant remains of anything.

clue.text: Charming setter wearing women's pants

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes sits inside them, so the setter goes inside the other letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word before it is rated poor and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter, rather charmingly, is dressed in ladies' trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like the garment being worn; it is the anagram signal, British slang for poor or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A winsome manner is appealing in an innocent, engaging way, the same as charming.

clue.text: Most beautiful female gets one place to raise a family

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the Roman numeral for one
birds rear their young in a nest

explanation.surface: A lovely woman acquires a home suitable for bringing up children.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine can mean handsome or attractive, so its superlative describes whoever is loveliest of all.

clue.text: Reprobate, said to go to pub, becoming bright red

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for a reprobate counts only for how it is pronounced

parts.note: a reprobate is a sinner
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A wicked person heads off to the pub and ends up flushed scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinna is a name from Roman history, but here it is only the sound of a word for a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a red mercury ore, and its name is used for the vivid scarlet pigment and colour.

clue.text: A man and I prepared to tuck into cheese from a large pan of hot water

definitions.text: a large pan of hot water

indicators.note: to tuck into food is to go inside it, so the rearranged letters sit within the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so these letters are made into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, link 'and' aside

explanation.surface: Two people get ready to eat cheese straight out of a big hot pan, like a fondue.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is A, MAN and I; the extra R comes from inside the cheese, which splits around the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a cooking vessel of hot water in which a smaller dish sits for gentle heating.

clue.text: Organ is in concluding part of performance

parts.note: a fish's fin is one of its organs
taken as written

explanation.surface: An organist plays in the closing section of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument; here it is a body part of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Finis is the Latin word printed at the close of a book or film, marking the end of a show.

clue.text: Verger's first to see vicar forced into reciprocal relationship

indicators.note: something forced is pushed out of its natural shape, so these letters are bent into new order
the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the verger is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Verger
the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A verger is first in line to meet a vicar who has been pushed into a mutual arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: A verger is a church officer who looks after the building and assists the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the other way round, describing a relationship where the same holds in both directions.

clue.text: Woman with very little money

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A woman who is nearly broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The British penny is one hundredth of a pound, the coin of least value.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a female first name and a tiny coin, standing for a trifling sum.

clue.text: Unite king and fool

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A call for a monarch and his jester to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knit as they heal, and people knit together when joined closely, so the verb means join.

clue.text: After a time, be inclined to go

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
to tend to do something is to be inclined to it

explanation.surface: Someone who, after a while, feels like leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the a-and-time letters first, ahead of the inclination word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event or institution, such as school or church, is to go there regularly.

clue.text: Crew visiting island by boat somehow reaching part of Canada

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters may be arranged in any order

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors visiting an island by boat somehow end up in a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' simply places the crew word beside the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the prairie provinces of central Canada, with Winnipeg as its capital.

clue.text: Mother strict with dog?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
stiff can mean severe or harsh

explanation.surface: A severe mother has a dog, or perhaps is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog with a heavy head.

clue.text: Ordered a Republican to rank Democrat

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
to range things is to rank or set them in order
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A Republican was told to grade a Democrat, as in American politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command given; it is the definition meaning set in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged has been organised or put into a set sequence, just as ordered items are.

clue.text: Arsonist originally restricted by appropriate court order

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so it goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Arsonist

explanation.surface: A fire-raiser is initially limited by a suitable judicial injunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command, such as one issued by a court or ruler.

clue.text: Official set off to battle with duke

indicators.note: off means not right, as food goes off, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a war is a battle in broad terms
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A functionary sets out for war alongside a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as one phrase meaning depart; 'off' is the anagram signal working on 'set' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who manages events, property or passengers on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: What bookies pay out after Worcestershire's first spell at the crease

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the county is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Worcestershire
a batsman's turn at the crease in cricket

explanation.surface: Bookmakers settle up after a county cricket team's first batting session.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire is an English county with a cricket team; the crease is where the batsman stands, so a spell there is a turn batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Money won on bets is collected from the bookmaker, so a punter's gains are what bookies hand over.

clue.text: Correct behaviour shown by English company during strike

indicators.note: during means within a span, so these letters fall inside the word for strike

parts.note: to drum is to beat or strike repeatedly
E is the abbreviation for English
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An English firm behaves properly while its workers are on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, dignified conduct that follows accepted standards of good taste.

clue.text: Cheat to win at end of simple card game

parts.note: to crib is to copy dishonestly
to bag something is to win or secure it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of simple is kept

parts.note: the final letter of simple

explanation.surface: Someone cheats to win a straightforward game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game for two to four players scored by moving pegs on a board.

clue.text: Argue with Hell's Angel about source of cannabis

indicators.note: about means around, so the motorcyclist wraps around the selected letter

parts.note: Hell's Angels are a motorcycle gang

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter of cannabis is used

parts.note: the opening letter of cannabis

explanation.surface: Quarrelling with a gang member over who supplied the dope.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble over trivial things, a petty kind of arguing.

clue.text: Cover what journalists write about article

indicators.note: about means around, so the journalists' word goes round the article

parts.note: copy is the text written for publication
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Reporters are told to cover a story about a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a journalist's instruction to report; it is the definition, a noun for a shelter overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering of fabric or foliage that shelters whatever lies beneath.

clue.text: Conservative party's flipping smart!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the party word is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation that a Tory party is flipping clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British intensifier, like damned; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and clever both describe someone quick-witted and intelligent.

clue.text: Clergymen in the army wanting tea in open country

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the tea word is taken out

parts.note: chaplains minister to soldiers
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Army padres out in the countryside are longing for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha, also spelt char, is British slang for tea and is removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Plains are wide, flat stretches of land with few trees, which is exactly open country.

clue.text: Small narrow part of latch

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the neck of a bottle is its narrow part

explanation.surface: Describing a slim, narrow piece of a door's catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of latch' looks like the definition; 'part' belongs to the wordplay and the definition is just 'latch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneck is a Scottish and northern English dialect word for a door latch or catch.

clue.text: Author of Blood very keen to return to Lima

indicators.note: to return is to come back round, so the first letter of the keen word travels round to its end

parts.note: gore is blood shed from a wound
avid means eager
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The writer of a book called Blood is eager to go back to the capital of Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author of Blood' reads as one title; 'of' is only a link. The A at the front of the keen word comes round to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was an American novelist and essayist, author of Myra Breckinridge and Burr.

clue.text: Speculate about Queen's headgear

indicators.note: about means around, so the betting word encloses the monarch's letters

parts.note: to bet is to gamble or speculate
the royal cipher ER, Elizabeth Regina, taken here with its letters in Latin order, Regina Elizabetha

explanation.surface: Gambling over what hat the Queen will wear.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the usual Queen; here her two letters appear the other way about, a liberty the setter takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a round, flat, soft cap, a kind of headgear associated with France and the army.

clue.text: Tavern getting hold of popular vegetable

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grasp it, so the tavern word wraps around the next

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An inn takes delivery of a well-liked vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is the British name for the purple eggplant, cooked and eaten as a vegetable.
